buildings.n: Ell Circo D'ell Fuego - Het Pakhuis

walls.note: Antwerp c.1650: the Spanish enceinte (1542-c.1567, the 'Spaanse omwalling'), the Scheldt front and the pentagonal citadel (1567-71), traced from the Ferraris map (1777), which shows them unchanged. Local metres around the Grote Markt (x east, z south). The ring follows the inner (curtain) line of the rampart on the land side; the projecting bastions and ravelins are not traced individually. The ring includes the citadel and the esplanade; the citadel's own enceinte is in forts[] (approximate, +-30 m). 'water' is the strip of the 17th-c. Scheldt between the old riverbank and today's quays (built 1877-85 on land reclaimed from the river).

landmarks.y1650: Cathedral (since 1559); the north tower, finished in 1518, about 123 m, was the highest in the Low Countries; the south tower stops at a third of its height.
landmarks.special: main bell tower; unfinished south tower

landmarks.footprintNote: position: centroid of the traced fort in walls/antwerpen.json
landmarks.y1650: Pentagonal citadel begun in 1567 by Alva south of the town (Paciotto); held by a Spanish garrison.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Antwerpen' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140031); nl.wikipedia 'Zuidkasteel'

landmarks.y1650: The old castle (burcht) on the Scheldt, prison in 1650.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Antwerpen' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140031)

landmarks.y1650: The irregular medieval Scheldt front with the Werf jutting out north of Het Steen and quays and water gates (straightened only in 1877-85).
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Antwerpen' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140031)

landmarks.y1650: Renaissance town hall of 1561-65 by Cornelis Floris.
